title: Grounder-Action Base Communication Protocol
rationale: Defines how Grounder retrieves conditions from Action Base and formats output for Ranker

step_1_input.description: Grounder receives interpreter output (NOT original query)

example.query_semantic: forecast vaccine side effects in Europe
example.description: User wants predictions of future adverse events

step_2_lookup.description: Grounder looks up action in Action Base

step_3_validation.description: Grounder validates action exists in AB

return_structure_if_invalid.error_message: Action {intended_action} not found in Action Base v1.0

step_4_output.description: Grounder returns structured conditions for Ranker

example_output.query_semantic: forecast vaccine side effects in Europe

grounder_pseudocode:
def ground_intent(interpreter_output, action_base):
    # Step 1: Extract intended action
    intended_action = interpreter_output['intended_action']
    
    # Step 2: Lookup in Action Base
    if intended_action in action_base['actions']:
        # Step 3: Retrieve conditions
        action_spec = action_base['actions'][intended_action]
        conditions = action_spec['conditions']
        
        # Step 4: Return formatted output
        return {
            'grounding_id': generate_id(),
            'query_semantic': interpreter_output['query_semantic'],
            'intended_action': intended_action,
            'action_found': True,
            'conditions': conditions,
            'timestamp': now()
        }
    else:
        # Action not found
        return {
            'grounding_id': generate_id(),
            'intended_action': intended_action,
            'action_found': False,
            'conditions': [],
            'error': f'Action {intended_action} not in Action Base',
            'timestamp': now()
        }
key_design_principles: No LLM needed - pure data lookup and extraction
Conditions are pre-authored in Action Base (not generated)
Each condition includes 'ranker_check' for Ranker to evaluate
Grounder is stateless and deterministic (same input = same output)

research_contribution.novelty: Separates intent grounding (finding what the user wants) from data ranking (finding which tables can do it)
research_contribution.rigor: Conditions are evaluable from schema, not theoretical assumptions
research_contribution.clarity: Action Base is explicit, version-controlled, auditable
research_contribution.extensibility: Easy to add new actions or conditions without code changes
